title: Hiring compact belief metrics and first 90d activation journal
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact hiring belief framework (what signals we actually care about when making an offer) and a lightweight, evidence-driven first-90d activation journal for new hires. Goal: reduce time-to-impact while keeping offer/hold decisions defensible and consistent across orgs.

Context and hypothesis:
- We see repeated variance in hiring outcomes: candidates who score highly on take-home tasks do not always translate to 60–90d impact.
- Hypothesis: aligning interview signal weightings with the first-30/60/90 activation requirements (project ownership, cross-team communication, debugging tempo) will reduce probation escalations.
- This doc is intentionally compact: minimal fields for interviewers to capture signal, and a short evidence journal template for managers to log activation checkpoints.

Compact hiring belief metrics (what we actually use) — single-line scorer fields for interviewers:
- Core craft (technical/problem decomposition): 1–5 (observable in pair/probe)
- Production-readiness intuition (shipping, observability): 1–5
- Collaboration bandwidth (async + sync): 1–5
- Learning velocity (how quickly they close feedback loops): 1–5
- Role fit signal (motivation & domain alignment): 1–5
- Risk flags: free text (data security, communication, ramp dependencies)
Notes on scoring: aim for 3+ for IC2/3 hires; 4+ for senior IC and IC4+ roles. Scores are guidance — the qualitative note must justify a score <=2.

Interview rubric (condensed cheat sheet for panel):
- 5 minutes: context + culture fit warmup (why Redwood inference, past shipping stories)
- 25 minutes: live probe (pair or take-home walkthrough) focusing on decomposition & tradeoffs
- 10 minutes: production questions (observability, monitoring, rollout decisions)
- 10 minutes: behavioral + collaboration (async comms sample, conflict story)
- Deliverable: fill the 6 fields above + one-line recommendation (Green/Amber/Red) and link to artifacts (take-home, PRs).

Offer decision floor and exceptions:
- Standard floor: at least 3 on Core craft and Collaboration AND overall avg >=3.5 for mid-senior roles.
- Exceptions: hiring manager must document compensating evidence in the offer memo (past ownership, internal referral, unique domain expertise).

First 90d activation journal (manager template — keep short, one-line entries):
- Week 0 (day 1 setup): access status, buddy assigned, first-week project brief, CI/CD access (Y/N), first-day blockers
- Week 1 checkpoints: 3 small tasks assigned, pair sessions scheduled, first async update sent to team (Y/N)
- End Week 2: project ticket ownership delegated, PR review loop established, mentor/peer feedback captured
- End Week 4 (30d): measurable output (merged PR/feature flag rollout) and 30d self-assessment + manager note
- End Week 8 (60d): independent story delivered, cross-team demo, quality/regression indicators
- End Week 12 (90d): probation evidence summary: impact examples, learning log, blocked areas, suggested next growth sprint

Evidence log example lines (one per date):
- 2026-02-12 | Task: onboard infra repo; Outcome: ready to run locally; Blockers: KMS creds; Owner note: mentor Asha helped with creds, unblock ETA 48h
- 2026-03-01 | Task: shipping incremental index optimizer; Outcome: PR merged behind ff; Observability: added basic traces; Manager note: shows pragmatic telemetry choices

Mentor pairing protocol (quick):
- Pair for first 10 working days (4–6 one-hour pairs). Aim: one pairing with platform engineer and one with product-facing engineer.
- Mentor notes: daily 15m async recap in a shared doc for first 2 weeks.
- Swap check: at day 30, both mentor and mentee rate fit (Keep / Reassign) with short rationale.

Probation decision matrix (simple):
- Green: clear impact examples at 30/60/90, no unresolved risk flags = confirm
- Amber: one moderate risk flag or delayed delivery; extend probation 30d with specific objectives
- Red: unresolved security or team-safety flags, or inability to show learning velocity = offboard discussion

Open questions / tradeoffs we still need to decide:
- How to weight take-home vs live pairing for remote candidates (current tilt: live pairing + take-home + PR review)
- Should we require explicit telemetry questions for all infra/platform roles? (pro: catches production readiness; con: longer interviews)
- Are interviewers overburdened by scoring? Can we move to binary flags + 1 free-text evidence line?

Next steps and owners (short actions):
- Pilot this compact form on five inbound mid-senior hires in Q2 2026 — owner: Nina (people-ops)
- Build a one-click Google Form for interviewers that emits the six fields + free text — owner: Diego Morales (1 week)
- Add a probation summary template to People Ops Confluence — owner: Asha Patel (2 weeks)
- Retrospective after pilot with hiring managers and SRE/product leads (collect 5 cases) — owner: Samir Zhang (end of pilot)

Notes to reviewers: please focus feedback on a) whether these signals capture early-impact, and b) whether the evidence log fields are low-friction in practice. If you disagree with floor thresholds, flag concrete alternatives with rationale.

Appendix (templates to copy into PM/Manager onboarding flow):
- Interview short form: six numeric fields, one-line recommendation, link to artifact, 1-sentence rationale for any score <=2.
- Manager 90d journal: date | task | outcome | blocker | manager note | next action.
summary: Compact hiring belief framework and a short manager-facing 90d activation journal to reduce probation variance. Pilot plan assigned to people-ops owners.
